f.title: Evaluate new benefit-risk information continuously after marketing, in consultation with regulators
f.statement: Once a product is marketed, new information that can have an impact on the benefits or risks of the product will be generated; evaluation of this information should be a continuing process, in consultation with regulatory authorities.

rows.quote:
Once a product is marketed, new information will be generated, which can have an
impact on the benefits or risks of the product; evaluation of this information should be a
continuing process, in consultation with regulatory authorities.
rows.review_note: Review: added missed expectation from 1.2 Background (should = Recommended). Double-check: 86: expectation sits in 1.2 Background and names no actor; 'Sponsor' is inferred (the evaluation is described as joint with regulators), so actor and normative weight need admin confirmation.

f.title: Involve company pharmacovigilance experts early in product development
f.statement: Company pharmacovigilance experts should get involved early in product development.

rows.quote: It is recommended that company pharmacovigilance experts get involved early in product development.
rows.review_note: Review: removed rationale not stated in the source from the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Start pharmacovigilance planning and dialogue with regulators long before licence application
f.statement: Planning of pharmacovigilance activities and dialogue with regulators should start long before the licence application is submitted.

rows.quote: Planning and dialogue with regulators should also start long before license application.

f.title: Optionally develop a Safety Specification and Pharmacovigilance Plan for marketed products
f.statement: A Safety Specification and Pharmacovigilance Plan can also be developed for products already on the market (e.g. new indication or major new safety concern). The Plan could be used as the basis for discussion of pharmacovigilance activities with regulators in the different ICH regions and beyond.
f.applicability: Products already on the market, e.g. new indication or major new safety concern

rows.quote:
A Safety Specification and Pharmacovigilance Plan can also
be developed for products already on the market (e.g., new indication or major new
safety concern). The Plan could be used as the basis for discussion of pharmacovigilance
activities with regulators in the different ICH regions and beyond.
rows.review_note: Review: added missed permission from 1.3 Scope (can/could = Permitted). Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Include additional actions in the Pharmacovigilance Plan for important risks or missing information
f.statement: For products with important identified risks, important potential risks or important missing information, the Pharmacovigilance Plan should include additional actions designed to address these concerns. For products for which no special concerns have arisen, routine pharmacovigilance (section 3.1.2) should be sufficient for post-approval safety monitoring without additional actions such as safety studies.
f.applicability: Products with important identified risks, important potential risks or important missing information
f.exceptions: Products with no special concerns: routine pharmacovigilance should be sufficient
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote:
For products with important identified risks, important potential risks or important
missing information, the Pharmacovigilance Plan should include additional actions
designed to address these concerns. For products for which no special concerns have
arisen, routine pharmacovigilance as described in section 3.1.2 should be sufficient for
post-approval safety monitoring, without the need for additional actions (e.g., safety
studies).
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: kept, not merged with ICH-E2E-0032: 1.3 Scope says the Plan 'should include' additional actions, while section 3 says they 'should be considered'; the two levels of expectation differ, so both rows stay and are cross-referenced. Row itself confirmed.

f.title: Revise the Pharmacovigilance Plan with important emerging benefit or risk information
f.statement: During implementation of the components of the Pharmacovigilance Plan, any important emerging benefit or risk information should be discussed and used to revise the Plan.

rows.quote:
During the course of implementing the various components of the Plan, any important
emerging benefit or risk information should be discussed and used to revise the Plan.

f.title: Summarise important identified risks, potential risks and missing information in the Safety Specification
f.statement: The Safety Specification should be a summary of the important identified risks of the drug, important potential risks and important missing information.

rows.quote:
The Safety Specification should be a summary of the important identified risks of a drug,
important potential risks, and important missing information.

f.title: Address at-risk populations and outstanding safety questions in the Safety Specification
f.statement: The Safety Specification should also address the populations potentially at risk (where the product is likely to be used) and outstanding safety questions that warrant further investigation to refine understanding of the benefit-risk profile during the post-approval period.

rows.quote:
It should also address the
populations potentially at-risk (where the product is likely to be used), and outstanding
safety questions which warrant further investigation to refine understanding of the
benefit-risk profile during the post-approval period.

f.title: Reflect the status of issues followed during development in the Safety Specification at approval
f.statement: The Safety Specification can be built initially during the pre-marketing phase; at the time approval is sought it should reflect the status of issues that were being followed during development.

rows.deadline: At the time approval is sought
rows.quote:
The Safety
Specification can be built initially during the pre-marketing phase and, at the time



                                            2
                                                                    Pharmacovigilance Planning



approval is sought, it should reflect the status of issues that were being followed during
development.

f.title: Base the Safety Specification safety issues on the CTD safety sections
f.statement: The safety information in the Common Technical Document, especially the Overview of Safety [2.5.5], Benefits and Risks Conclusions [2.5.6] and Summary of Clinical Safety [2.7.4], should be the basis of the safety issues identified in the Safety Specification.

rows.quote:
The Common Technical Document (CTD), especially the Overview of Safety [2.5.5],
Benefits and Risks Conclusions [2.5.6], and the Summary of Clinical Safety [2.7.4]
sections, includes information relating to the safety of the product, and should be the
basis of the safety issues identified in the Safety Specification.

f.title: Support the Safety Specification with references to specific CTD pages
f.statement: Sponsors should support the Safety Specification with references to specific pages of the CTD or other relevant documents.

rows.quote:
Sponsors should support
the Safety Specification with references to specific pages of the CTD or other relevant
documents.
rows.review_note: Review: moved the stand-alone/CTD/appendix format options (not proven by this quote) to new Permitted row ICH-E2E-0071. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Optionally present the Safety Specification stand-alone or within the CTD, with appendices
f.statement: The Safety Specification can be a stand-alone document, usually in conjunction with the Pharmacovigilance Plan, but elements can also be incorporated into the CTD. Its length will generally depend on the product and its development program, and appendices can be added if it is considered important to provide a more detailed explanation of important risks or analyses.

rows.quote:
The Safety Specification can be a stand-alone document, usually in
conjunction with the Pharmacovigilance Plan, but elements can also be incorporated into
the CTD. The length of the document will generally depend on the product and its
development program. Appendices can be added if it is considered important to provide a
more detailed explanation of important risks or analyses.
rows.review_note: Review: added as separate Permitted row; content was previously folded into ICH-E2E-0009 without quote support. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Follow the recommended structure of elements when compiling the Safety Specification
f.statement: Sponsors should follow the structure of elements in section 2.1 when compiling the Safety Specification. The elements are only a guide: additional elements can be included depending on the product and its development program, and for marketed products with emerging new safety concerns only a subset may be relevant.
f.exceptions: Additional elements can be included; for marketed products with emerging new safety concerns only a subset of elements might be relevant

rows.quote:
It is recommended that sponsors follow the structure of elements provided below when
compiling the Safety Specification. The elements of the Safety Specification that are
included are only a guide. The Safety Specification can include additional elements,
depending on the nature of the product and its development program. Conversely, for
products already on the market with emerging new safety concerns, only a subset of the
elements might be relevant.
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover the flexibility conditions stated in the statement and exceptions. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Focus the Safety Specification on identified risks, important potential risks and missing information
f.statement: The focus of the Safety Specification should be on the identified risks, important potential risks and important missing information, and the elements in section 2.1 should be considered for inclusion.

rows.quote:
The focus of the Safety Specification should be on the identified risks, important
potential risks, and important missing information. The following elements should be
considered for inclusion.

f.title: Present non-clinical safety findings not adequately addressed by clinical data
f.statement: The non-clinical section of the Safety Specification should present non-clinical safety findings that have not been adequately addressed by clinical data, for example toxicity (repeat-dose, reproductive/developmental, nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity etc.), general pharmacology (cardiovascular including QT prolongation, nervous system etc.), drug interactions and other toxicity-related information or data.

rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the listed examples used in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Consider specific non-clinical data needs for special populations
f.statement: If the product is intended for use in special populations, consideration should be given to whether specific non-clinical data needs exist.
f.applicability: Products intended for use in special populations

rows.quote:
If the product is intended for use in special populations, consideration should be given to
whether specific non-clinical data needs exist.

f.title: Discuss limitations of the human safety database and their implications
f.statement: Limitations of the human safety database (e.g. size of the study population, inclusion/exclusion criteria) should be considered, and the implications of these limitations for predicting the safety of the product in the marketplace should be explicitly discussed, with particular reference to populations likely to be exposed during intended or expected use in medical practice.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, a. Limitations of the Human Safety Database
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
Limitations of the safety database (e.g., related to the size of the study population, study
inclusion/exclusion criteria) should be considered, and the implications of such
limitations with respect to predicting the safety of the product in the marketplace should
be explicitly discussed. Particular reference should be made to populations likely to be
exposed during the intended or expected use of the product in medical practice.
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, a. Limitations of the Human Safety Database

f.title: Briefly discuss world-wide experience with the product
f.statement: The world-wide experience should be briefly discussed, including the extent of world-wide exposure, any new or different safety issues identified and any regulatory actions related to safety.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, a. Limitations of the Human Safety Database

rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, a. Limitations of the Human Safety Database

f.title: Discuss populations not studied or studied to a limited degree pre-approval
f.statement: The Safety Specification should discuss which populations have not been studied, or only to a limited degree, in the pre-approval phase and explicitly discuss the implications for predicting safety in the marketplace (CTD 2.5.5). Populations to be considered should include, but might not be limited to: children; the elderly; pregnant or lactating women; patients with relevant co-morbidity such as hepatic or renal disorders; patients with disease severity different from that studied in clinical trials; sub-populations carrying known and relevant genetic polymorphism; and patients of different racial and/or ethnic origins.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, b. Populations not Studied in the Pre-Approval Phase
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, b. Populations not Studied in the Pre-Approval Phase
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the listed populations used in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: List important identified and potential risks requiring further evaluation, with CTD references
f.statement: The AE/ADR section should list the important identified and potential risks that require further characterisation or evaluation, with specific references guiding a reviewer to where clinical safety data are presented (e.g. CTD 2.5.5 and 2.7.4).
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Adverse Events (AEs) / Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)

rows.quote:
This section should list the important identified and potential risks that require further
characterisation or evaluation. Specific references should be made to guide a reviewer to
where clinical safety data are presented (e.g., relevant sections of the CTD 2.5.5 and
2.7.4).
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Adverse Events (AEs) / Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)

f.title: Draw on all CTD and other relevant information when discussing risk factors and mechanisms
f.statement: Discussion of risk factors and potential mechanisms for identified AEs/ADRs should draw on information from any part of the CTD (non-clinical and clinical) and other relevant information, such as other drug labels, scientific literature and post-marketing experience.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Adverse Events (AEs) / Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)

rows.quote:
Discussion of risk factors and potential mechanisms that apply to identified AEs/ADRs
should draw on information from any part of the CTD (non-clinical and clinical) and
other relevant information, such as other drug labels, scientific literature, and post-
marketing experience.
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Adverse Events (AEs) / Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)

f.title: Provide detailed information on the most important identified AEs/ADRs
f.statement: More detailed information should be included on the most important identified AEs/ADRs, including those that are serious or frequent and that also might affect the benefit-risk balance. This should include evidence bearing on causal relationship, severity, seriousness, frequency, reversibility and at-risk groups, if available, and risk factors and potential mechanisms should be discussed.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Identified risks that require further evaluation

rows.quote:
More detailed information should be included on the most important identified
AEs/ADRs, which would include those that are serious or frequent and that also might
have an impact on the balance of benefits and risks of the product. This information
should include evidence bearing on a causal relationship, severity, seriousness,
frequency, reversibility and at-risk groups, if available. Risk factors and potential
mechanisms should be discussed.
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Identified risks that require further evaluation
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: changed 'i.e.' to 'including' (source says the most important AEs/ADRs 'would include' serious or frequent ones, not limited to them); confirmed.

f.title: Plan further evaluation of the most important identified AEs/ADRs in the Pharmacovigilance Plan
f.statement: The most important identified AEs/ADRs should usually call for further evaluation as part of the Pharmacovigilance Plan (e.g. frequency in normal conditions of use, severity, outcome, at-risk groups).
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Identified risks that require further evaluation
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote:
These AEs/ADRs should usually call for further
evaluation as part of the Pharmacovigilance Plan (e.g., frequency in normal conditions of
use, severity, outcome, at-risk groups, etc.).
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Identified risks that require further evaluation

f.title: Describe important potential risks and present the supporting evidence
f.statement: Important potential risks should be described, and the evidence that led to the conclusion that there was a potential risk should be presented.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Potential risks that require further evaluation

rows.quote:
Important potential risks should be described in this section. The evidence that led to
the conclusion that there was a potential risk should be presented.
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Potential risks that require further evaluation

f.title: Further evaluate each important potential risk to characterise the association
f.statement: For any important potential risk there should be further evaluation to characterise the association.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Potential risks that require further evaluation
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote:
It is anticipated that
for any important potential risk, there should be further evaluation to characterise the
association.
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, c. Potential risks that require further evaluation

f.title: Discuss identified and potential PK/PD interactions, their evidence, mechanism and health risks
f.statement: Identified and potential pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions, including food-drug and drug-drug interactions, should be discussed. For each, the supporting evidence and possible mechanism should be summarised, and the potential health risks for the different indications and populations should be discussed.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Clinical, d. Identified and Potential Interactions, Including Food-Drug and Drug-Drug Interactions

rows.quote:
Identified and Potential Interactions, Including Food-Drug and Drug-
        Drug Interactions
Identified and potential pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions should be
discussed. For each, the evidence supporting the interaction and possible mechanism
should be summarised, and the potential health risks posed for the different indications
and in the different populations should be discussed.
rows.location: 2.1.2 Clinical, d. Identified and Potential Interactions, Including Food-Drug and Drug-Drug Interactions
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: extended quote to the section heading so 'including food-drug and drug-drug interactions' in the statement is proven; confirmed.

f.title: Discuss the epidemiology of the indication with stratification
f.statement: The epidemiology of the indication(s) should be discussed, including incidence, prevalence, mortality and relevant co-morbidity, taking into account whenever possible stratification by age, sex and racial and/or ethnic origin.
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote:
The epidemiology of the indication(s) should be discussed. This discussion should include
incidence, prevalence, mortality and relevant co-morbidity, and should take into account
whenever possible stratification by age, sex, and racial and/or ethnic origin.

f.title: Discuss regional differences in the epidemiology of the indication
f.statement: Differences in the epidemiology of the indication(s) across regions should be discussed, if this information is available.
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote:
Differences
in the epidemiology in the different regions should be discussed (because the
epidemiology of the indication(s) may vary across regions), if this information is
available.

f.title: Review background incidence rates and risk factors for important adverse events
f.statement: For important adverse events that may require further investigation, it is useful to review the background incidence rates of these events among patients in whom the drug is indicated but who are not treated with it, and to include information on risk factors for the adverse event, if available.
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote:
In addition, for important adverse events that may require further investigation, it is
useful to review the incidence rates of these events among patients in whom the drug is
indicated (i.e., the background incidence rates). For example, if condition X is an
important adverse event in patients who are treated with drug Y for disease Z, then it is
useful to review the incidence of condition X in patients with disease Z who are not
treated with drug Y; this is the background rate of condition X among patients with
disease Z. Information on risk factors for an adverse event (condition X) would also be
useful to include, if available.
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover the background-rate example and risk-factor information used in the statement. Double-check: 84: source says it 'is useful' to review background incidence rates, which is advisory rather than a clear 'should'; level Recommended is arguable (could be Permitted).

f.title: Identify risks common to the pharmacological class
f.statement: The Safety Specification should identify risks believed to be common to the pharmacological class.

rows.quote:
The Safety Specification should identify risks believed to be common to the
pharmacological class.

f.title: Provide a summary of important risks and missing information at the end of the Safety Specification
f.statement: At the end of the Safety Specification a summary should be provided of the important identified risks, important potential risks and important missing information.

f.title: Summarise ongoing safety issues issue by issue
f.statement: Sponsors are encouraged to summarise specific ongoing safety issues on an issue-by-issue basis, including both non-clinical and clinical data pertinent to the problem.

rows.quote:
Sponsors are encouraged to summarise specific ongoing safety issues on an issue-by-
issue basis, including both non-clinical and clinical data that are pertinent to the
problem.

f.title: Base the Pharmacovigilance Plan on the Safety Specification
f.statement: The Pharmacovigilance Plan should be based on the Safety Specification. The Specification and Plan can be written as two parts of the same document.

rows.quote:
Pharmacovigilance Plan should be based on the Safety Specification. The Specification
and Plan can be written as two parts of the same document.
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover the second sentence of the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Discuss the Pharmacovigilance Plan with regulators during development, at submission or post-marketing
f.statement: The Pharmacovigilance Plan would normally be developed by the sponsor and can be discussed with regulators during product development, prior to approval (i.e. when the marketing application is submitted) of a new product, or when a safety concern arises post-marketing. It can be a stand-alone document or elements can be incorporated into the CTD.

rows.quote:
The Plan would normally be
developed by the sponsor and can be discussed with regulators during product
development, prior to approval (i.e., when the marketing application is submitted) of a
new product, or when a safety concern arises post-marketing. It can be a stand-alone
document but elements could also be incorporated into the CTD.

f.title: Consider additional actions beyond routine pharmacovigilance for important risks or missing information
f.statement: For products with no special concerns, routine pharmacovigilance (section 3.1.2) should be sufficient for post-approval safety monitoring without additional actions such as safety studies. For products with important identified risks, important potential risks or important missing information, additional actions designed to address these concerns should be considered.
f.applicability: Products with important identified risks, important potential risks or important missing information
f.exceptions: Products with no special concerns: routine pharmacovigilance should be sufficient
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote:
For products for which no special concerns have arisen, routine pharmacovigilance as
described in section 3.1.2 should be sufficient for post-approval safety monitoring,


                                            5
 Pharmacovigilance Planning



without the need for additional actions (e.g., safety studies). However, for products with
important identified risks, important potential risks, or important missing information,
additional actions designed to address these concerns should be considered.
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover the routine-pharmacovigilance sentence in the statement; kept separate from ICH-E2E-0003 because section 3 sets a weaker expectation ("should be considered") than section 1.3 ("should include"). Double-check: 88: kept as a separate row from ICH-E2E-0003 (section 3 'should be considered' is weaker than 1.3 'should include'), but the routine-pharmacovigilance sentence duplicates ICH-E2E-0003 and ICH-E2E-0036; admin should confirm whether the library wants both near-duplicate rows.

f.title: Update the Pharmacovigilance Plan as important safety information emerges and milestones are reached
f.statement: The Pharmacovigilance Plan should be updated as important information on safety becomes available and as milestones are reached.

rows.deadline: As important safety information becomes available and milestones are reached
rows.quote:
The Pharmacovigilance Plan should be updated as important information on
safety becomes available and milestones are reached.

f.title: Adapt the suggested Pharmacovigilance Plan structure to the product and issues
f.statement: The suggested structure for the Pharmacovigilance Plan can be varied depending on the product in question and the issues identified in the Safety Specification.

rows.quote:
The structure
can be varied depending on the product in question and the issues identified in the
Safety Specification.

f.title: Start the Pharmacovigilance Plan with a summary of ongoing safety issues
f.statement: At the beginning of the Pharmacovigilance Plan a summary should be provided of the important identified risks, important potential risks and important missing information. This is important if the Plan is a separate document from the Safety Specification.

rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: extended quote to the last sentence ('important if the Plan is a separate document'), which the statement used without support; confirmed.

f.title: Conduct routine pharmacovigilance for all medicinal products
f.statement: Routine pharmacovigilance should be conducted for all medicinal products, regardless of whether additional actions are appropriate as part of a Pharmacovigilance Plan.

rows.quote:
Routine pharmacovigilance should be conducted for all medicinal products, regardless of
whether or not additional actions are appropriate as part of a Pharmacovigilance Plan.

f.title: Maintain systems to collect and collate all suspected adverse reactions reported to company personnel
f.statement: Routine pharmacovigilance should include systems and processes that ensure information about all suspected adverse reactions reported to company personnel is collected and collated in an accessible manner.
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up; Safety system configuration

f.title: Prepare expedited ADR reports and PSURs for regulatory authorities
f.statement: Routine pharmacovigilance should include the preparation of reports for regulatory authorities: expedited adverse drug reaction (ADR) reports and Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs).

f.title: Continuously monitor the safety profile of approved products
f.statement: Routine pharmacovigilance should include continuous monitoring of the safety profile of approved products, including signal detection, issue evaluation, updating of labeling and liaison with regulatory authorities.
f.processes: Signal detection; Signal management; Safety labeling; Submission operations

f.title: Meet other routine pharmacovigilance requirements defined by local regulations
f.statement: Routine pharmacovigilance should also include other requirements as defined by local regulations.

rows.quote: Other requirements, as defined by local regulations.

f.title: Include in the Plan an overview of the PV organisation where regionally required, otherwise a statement on routine practices
f.statement: Some ICH regions might have a regulatory requirement to present within the Pharmacovigilance Plan an overview of the company's organisation and practices for conducting pharmacovigilance. In the absence of such a requirement, a statement in the Plan that the company's routine pharmacovigilance practices include the elements of section 3.1.2 (collection and collation of suspected adverse reactions, expedited ADR reports and PSURs, continuous safety monitoring, other local requirements) should be sufficient.
f.exceptions: Where a regional regulatory requirement exists, the overview of the company's organisation and practices is presented instead of the statement

rows.quote:
In some ICH regions, there might be a regulatory requirement to present within the
Pharmacovigilance Plan an overview of the company’s organisation and practices for
conducting pharmacovigilance. In the absence of such a requirement, a statement that
the company’s routine pharmacovigilance practices include the elements outlined in the
bulleted list above should be sufficient.
rows.review_note: Review: reworded statement to match the source (the guideline does not itself recommend the overview; it notes a possible regional requirement and says a statement suffices otherwise); adjusted applicability and exceptions. Double-check: 84: the source mainly notes a possible regional requirement and that a statement 'should be sufficient' otherwise; this is an acceptance/sufficiency statement rather than a clear duty, so the Recommended level and the psmf process mapping are judgement calls.

f.title: Present and justify an action plan for each important safety issue
f.statement: The Plan for each important safety issue should be presented and justified using the structure: safety issue; objective of proposed action(s); action(s) proposed; rationale for proposed action(s); monitoring by the sponsor for the safety issue and proposed action(s); milestones for evaluation and reporting.
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the structure elements listed in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Provide protocols for specific studies in the appropriate CTD sections
f.statement: Protocols for specific studies can be provided in CTD section 5.3.5.4 Other Clinical Study Reports or other sections as appropriate (e.g. Module 4 for a non-clinical study).

rows.quote:
Any protocols for specific studies can be provided in the CTD section 5.3.5.4 Other
Clinical Study Reports or other sections as appropriate (e.g., Module 4 if the study is a
non-clinical study).

f.title: Present an overall Pharmacovigilance Plan organised by actions and milestones
f.statement: An overall Pharmacovigilance Plan bringing together the actions for all individual safety issues should be presented, organised in terms of the actions to be undertaken and their milestones, since one proposed action (e.g. a prospective safety cohort study) could address more than one issue.
f.clause: 3.1.4 Summary of Actions to be Completed, Including Milestones

rows.quote:
An overall Pharmacovigilance Plan for the product bringing together the actions for all
individual safety issues should be presented. Whereas section 3.1.3 suggests presenting
an action plan by ongoing safety issue, for this section the Pharmacovigilance Plan for
the product should be organised in terms of the actions to be undertaken and their
milestones. The reason for this is that one proposed action (e.g., a prospective safety
cohort study) could address more than one of the identified issues.
rows.location: 3.1.4 Summary of Actions to be Completed, Including Milestones
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover organisation by actions and milestones stated in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Include milestones for study completion, evaluations and submission of safety results
f.statement: Milestones for completion of studies and other evaluations, and for submission of safety results, should be included in the Pharmacovigilance Plan. In developing these milestones, consideration should be given to when exposure to the product will have reached a level sufficient to allow potential identification/characterisation of the AEs/ADRs of concern or resolution of a particular concern, and/or when the results of ongoing or proposed safety studies are expected to be available.
f.clause: 3.1.4 Summary of Actions to be Completed, Including Milestones

rows.quote:
It is recommended that milestones for completion of studies and other evaluations, and
for submission of safety results, be included in the Pharmacovigilance Plan. In
developing these milestones one should consider when:
   •   Exposure to the product will have reached a level sufficient to allow potential
       identification/characterisation of the AEs/ADRs of concern or resolution of a
       particular concern; and/or
   •   The results of ongoing or proposed safety studies are expected to be available.
rows.location: 3.1.4 Summary of Actions to be Completed, Including Milestones
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the milestone considerations; aligned statement wording to the source. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Align Pharmacovigilance Plan milestones with regulatory milestones and use them to revise the Plan
f.statement: Pharmacovigilance Plan milestones might be aligned with regulatory milestones (e.g. PSURs, annual reassessment and licence renewals) and used to revise the Plan.
f.clause: 3.1.4 Summary of Actions to be Completed, Including Milestones

rows.quote:
These milestones might be aligned with regulatory milestones (e.g., PSURs, annual
reassessment and license renewals) and used to revise the Pharmacovigilance Plan.
rows.location: 3.1.4 Summary of Actions to be Completed, Including Milestones

f.title: Employ the most appropriate design to address a safety concern
f.statement: When choosing a method to address a safety concern, sponsors should employ the most appropriate design, taking into account the product, indication, population, the issue (identified risk, potential risk or missing information) and whether signal detection, evaluation or safety demonstration is the main objective.
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote:
The best method to address a specific situation can vary depending on the product, the
indication, the population being treated and the issue to be addressed. The method
chosen can also depend on whether an identified risk, potential risk or missing
information is the issue and whether signal detection, evaluation or safety
demonstration is the main objective of further study. When choosing a method to
address a safety concern, sponsors should employ the most appropriate design.
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover the selection factors listed in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Use the most up-to-date relevant pharmacovigilance methods
f.statement: The Annex list of methods is not all-inclusive, and sponsors should use the most up-to-date methods that are relevant and applicable.

rows.quote:
This list is not all-inclusive, and sponsors should
use the most up-to-date methods that are relevant and applicable.

f.title: Finalise the protocol before an observational study in the Pharmacovigilance Plan commences
f.statement: Before an observational study that is part of a Pharmacovigilance Plan commences, a protocol should be finalised.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies
f.applicability: Observational studies that are part of a Pharmacovigilance Plan

rows.quote:
Before the observational study that is part of a Pharmacovigilance Plan commences, a
protocol should be finalised.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Consult experts from relevant disciplines on observational studies
f.statement: Experts from relevant disciplines (e.g. pharmacovigilance experts, pharmacoepidemiologists and biostatisticians) should be consulted on observational studies that are part of a Pharmacovigilance Plan.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies
f.applicability: Observational studies that are part of a Pharmacovigilance Plan

rows.quote:
Experts from relevant disciplines (e.g., pharmacovigilance
experts, pharmacoepidemiologists and biostatisticians) should be consulted.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Discuss the observational study protocol with regulatory authorities before the study starts
f.statement: The observational study protocol should be discussed with the regulatory authorities before the study starts.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

rows.quote:
It is
recommended that the protocol be discussed with the regulatory authorities before the
study starts.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Discuss and document in advance the circumstances for early study termination
f.statement: The circumstances in which an observational study should be terminated early should be discussed with regulatory authorities and documented in advance.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

rows.quote:
It is also suggested that the circumstances in which a study should be
terminated early be discussed with regulatory authorities and documented in advance.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Submit observational study final and interim reports per Pharmacovigilance Plan milestones
f.statement: A study report after completion, and interim reports if appropriate, should be submitted to the authorities according to the milestones within the Pharmacovigilance Plan.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

rows.deadline: According to the milestones within the Pharmacovigilance Plan
rows.quote:
A study report after completion, and interim reports if appropriate, should be submitted
to the authorities according to the milestones within the Pharmacovigilance Plan.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Include minimum content in observational study protocols
f.statement: Study protocols should, as a minimum, include the study aims and objectives, the methods to be used and the plan for analysis.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

rows.quote:
Study protocols should, as a minimum, include the study aims and objectives, the
methods to be used, and the plan for analysis.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Present objectives, methods, results and interpretation accurately in the final study report
f.statement: The final study report should accurately and completely present the study objectives, methods, results and the principal investigator's interpretation of the findings.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

rows.quote:
The final study report should accurately
and completely present the study objectives, methods, results, and the principal
investigator’s interpretation of the findings.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Follow good epidemiological practice and internationally accepted guidelines for observational studies
f.statement: The sponsor should follow good epidemiological practice for observational studies and internationally accepted guidelines, such as those endorsed by the International Society for Pharmacoepidemiology.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote:
It is recommended that the sponsor follow good epidemiological practice for
observational studies and also internationally accepted guidelines, such as the
guidelines endorsed by the International Society for Pharmacoepidemiology.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Follow local laws and guidelines on observational study design and conduct
f.statement: In ICH regions where local laws and guidelines apply to the design and conduct of observational studies, they should be followed.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies
f.applicability: ICH regions with local laws and guidelines on observational studies
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Local PV interfaces

rows.quote:
In some of
the ICH regions, local laws and guidelines also apply to the design and conduct of
observational studies and should be followed.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Maintain professional conduct and confidentiality and follow data protection legislation
f.statement: The highest possible standards of professional conduct and confidentiality should always be maintained in observational studies, and any relevant national legislation on data protection should be followed.
f.clause: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Data integrity & records

rows.quote:
The highest possible standards of professional conduct and confidentiality should always
be maintained and any relevant national legislation on data protection followed.
rows.location: 3.2.1 Design and Conduct of Observational Studies

f.title: Exercise caution when evaluating spontaneous reports, especially when comparing drugs
f.statement: Caution should be exercised in evaluating spontaneous reports, especially when comparing drugs. The data accompanying spontaneous reports are often incomplete, and the rate at which cases are reported depends on many factors, including the time since launch, pharmacovigilance-related regulatory activity, media attention and the indication for use of the drug.

rows.quote:
Caution should be exercised in evaluating spontaneous reports,
       especially when comparing drugs. The data accompanying spontaneous reports
       are often incomplete, and the rate at which cases are reported is dependent on
       many factors including the time since launch, pharmacovigilance-related
       regulatory activity, media attention, and the indication for use of the drug.
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover the reasons (incomplete data, reporting-rate factors) stated in the statement. Double-check: reworded statement to drop the added causal 'because' and list the factors as the source states them; confirmed.

f.title: Use data mining alongside, not instead of, single case report analysis
f.statement: Data mining techniques should always be used in conjunction with, and not in place of, analyses of single case reports.
f.clause: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports

rows.quote:
Data mining techniques should always be used in conjunction with, and not in
       place of, analyses of single case reports.
rows.location: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports

f.title: Exercise caution when comparing drugs using data mining results
f.statement: Data mining does not quantify the magnitude of risk, and caution should be exercised when comparing drugs using it.
f.clause: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports

rows.quote:
This tool does not quantify the magnitude of risk,
       and caution should be exercised when comparing drugs.
rows.location: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports
rows.review_note: Review: split; the signal threshold consideration moved to new row ICH-E2E-0072; classification narrowed to signal evaluation. Double-check: removed inferred 'because' linkage to mirror the source; confirmed.

f.title: Consider the signal detection threshold when using data mining
f.statement: When using data mining techniques, consideration should be given to the threshold established for detecting signals, since this will have implications for the sensitivity and specificity of the method (a high threshold is associated with high specificity and low sensitivity).
f.clause: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports

rows.quote:
Further, when using
       data mining techniques, consideration should be given to the threshold
       established for detecting signals, since this will have implications for the
       sensitivity and specificity of the method (a high threshold is associated with high
       specificity and low sensitivity).
rows.location: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports
rows.review_note: Review: split from ICH-E2E-0061 (one duty per row). Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Interpret data mining results with knowledge of spontaneous reporting weaknesses
f.statement: Results of data mining should be interpreted with knowledge of the weaknesses of the spontaneous reporting system, in particular the large differences in ADR reporting rates among drugs and the many potential biases inherent in spontaneous reporting; confounding factors are not removed by data mining.
f.clause: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports

rows.quote:
Confounding factors that influence spontaneous
       adverse event reporting are not removed by data mining. Results of data mining
       should be interpreted with the knowledge of the weaknesses of the spontaneous
       reporting system and, more specifically, the large differences in the ADR
       reporting rate among different drugs and the many potential biases inherent in
       spontaneous reporting.
rows.location: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to cover the confounding-factors clause in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Evaluate all signals recognising the possibility of false positives
f.statement: All signals should be evaluated recognising the possibility of false positives; the absence of a signal does not mean that a problem does not exist.
f.clause: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports

rows.quote:
All signals should be evaluated recognising the possibility
       of false positives. In addition, the absence of a signal does not mean that a
       problem does not exist.
rows.location: Annex 1. Passive Surveillance - Systematic Methods for the Evaluation of Spontaneous Reports

f.title: Prioritise detailed and rapid follow-up of spontaneous reports of drug-associated distinct events
f.statement: For distinct adverse events known to be associated more frequently with drug therapy, such as anaphylaxis, aplastic anaemia, toxic epidermal necrolysis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome, sponsors should place more emphasis on spontaneous reports of these events for detailed and rapid follow-up.
f.applicability: Spontaneous reports of anaphylaxis, aplastic anaemia, toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and similar events

rows.quote:
There are

                                             9
 Pharmacovigilance Planning



       certain distinct adverse events known to be associated more frequently with drug
       therapy, such as anaphylaxis, aplastic anemia, toxic epidermal necrolysis and
       Stevens-Johnson Syndrome10,11. Therefore, when events such as these are
       spontaneously reported, sponsors should place more emphasis on these reports
       for detailed and rapid follow-up.
rows.review_note: Review: extended quote to include the named event examples used in the statement. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Optionally plan stimulated reporting for the early post-marketing phase before launch
f.statement: During the early post-marketing phase, companies might actively provide health professionals with safety information while encouraging cautious use of new products and the submission of spontaneous reports when an adverse event is identified; a plan can be developed before the product is launched (e.g. through site visits by company representatives, direct mailings or faxes).

rows.quote:
During the early post-marketing phase, companies might actively provide health
professionals with safety information, and at the same time encourage cautious use of
new products and the submission of spontaneous reports when an adverse event is
identified. A plan can be developed before the product is launched (e.g., through site
visits by company representatives, by direct mailings or faxes, etc.).
rows.review_note: Review: no change Double-check: extended quote to the examples (site visits, mailings, faxes) used in the statement, which the old quote cut off; confirmed.

f.title: Treat stimulated reports as spontaneous reports; do not derive incidence rates from them
f.statement: Stimulated adverse event reporting should be regarded as a form of spontaneous reporting; data from stimulated reporting cannot be used to generate accurate incidence rates, but reporting rates can be estimated.
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Signal detection; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote:
This should be regarded as a form of spontaneous event reporting, and thus data
obtained from stimulated reporting cannot be used to generate accurate incidence rates,
but reporting rates can be estimated.

f.title: Select case-control study controls representative of exposure in the source population
f.statement: In a case-control study, controls should be selected so that the prevalence of exposure among the controls represents the prevalence of exposure in the source population that gave rise to the cases.
f.clause: Annex 4. Comparative Observational Studies - Case-Control Study

rows.quote:
The controls should be selected in
       such a way that the prevalence of exposure among the controls represents the
       prevalence of exposure in the source population.
rows.location: Annex 4. Comparative Observational Studies - Case-Control Study

f.title: Respect privacy and confidentiality regulations when using patient medical records
f.statement: When medical records are used to ascertain and validate test results and diagnoses in database studies, one should be cognizant of the privacy and confidentiality regulations that apply to patient medical records.

Although medical records can be used

       cognizant of the privacy and confidentiality regulations that apply to patient
